title: Deterministic positive edge-weight limits for trace-reinforced ants on two parallel paths each of length at least two
source_title: The trace-reinforced ants process does not find shortest paths
author: Daniel Kious; Cécile Mailler; Bruno Schapira
difficulty_reason: General stochastic-approximation results do not rule out the boundary faces or identify a unique interior limit for this conductance-driven reinforcement process. The authors use stopped-time urn couplings to retain every path edge, then recursively enclose the limit set through monotone nonlinear conductance maps. The scalar contraction and uniqueness analysis determines the exact deterministic powers on both paths.
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.188

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.5 on the(p,q)-path graph, integers p,q>=2, initial weight1 on every edge, each N-to-F walk reinforced once per traversed edge rather than per crossing or loop-erased path. Limits are alpha^k/beta^ell with the unique interior solution of alpha^p+beta^q=1 and alpha^p(1-alpha)=beta^q(1-beta). Full new positive-weight induction, conductance vector field, nested order boxes, stochastic-approximation attraction and scalar contraction proof read. Existing Pemantle urn convergence and Benaim stochastic-approximation limit-set theorem are explicitly cited research foundations. Exact identity W_ap+W_bq=n+2 precedes the minor normalized hyperplane offset typo on21; either stated permitted n+2 normalization or its vanishing O(1/n) remainder in Definition2.3 gives the same displayed limiting hyperplane. Lemma5.3 prints fp-prime instead of its absolute value and the concluding endpoint as phi(0); the supplied derivative/polynomial monotonicity calculation establishes nonnegativity using phi(1)=0, a bounded ancillary scalar verification, not a new stochastic argument. No general-graph deterministic-limit conjecture, tree-like direct-edge assertion or cone/lozenge parameter variant counted separately.
